title: Rebuilding the web for agents — Liad Yosef, MCP Apps
talk_summary: Speaker describes MCP Apps and the 'agentic web': agents become entry points, websites expose headless tools/UI resources, and discovery/readiness standards emerge. The concrete evidence is from website-readiness scans: llm.txt is widely published but rarely used by agents, and agent paths vary by harness.

takeaways.what_they_do: They ran agents against websites and recorded the paths agents took; found agents mostly went to docs/homepage, not llm.txt, unless docs pointed to it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: almost 50% of the website that we tested that we ran published lms.txt but none of the agents that we ran on this website actually used llm.txt txt
takeaways.numbers: ~50% published llm.txt; none of tested agents used it; 40% used it only when docs pointed to it

takeaways.what_they_do: They run the same intent with Claude Code, Eve, and ChatGPT and compare agent journeys to see why outcomes differ.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we did it tens of thousands of times just to understand what agents really look for

takeaways.technique: Test tool descriptions against current models
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue static best practices for MCP/tool descriptions go stale as models improve; use agent feedback instead of human-authored standards.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every time they publish best practices, the models become better and these practices become obsolete
